riddle: In Hogwarts, this creature causes chaos in code. Hagrid might love it, but developers squash it daily.
hint: It rhymes with 'mug' and hides in your program.

riddle: Like the One Ring that circles endlessly until cast into Mount Doom, in code I repeat instructions until a condition sets me free.
hint: Think of something circular — for, while, do... it runs and repeats.

riddle: Nagini speaks it, Voldemort commands it in Parseltongue. In the coding world, it's one of the most popular languages — named after a reptile and a comedy troupe.
hint: Guido van Rossum created it. Famous for indentation and readability.

riddle: In Middle-earth, Gandalf roars 'You shall not pass!' In code, this keyword checks a condition — if it's true, you pass; if not, you take another path.
hint: Two letters. The most basic decision-making keyword: __ / else.

riddle: Like a Horcrux splits Voldemort's soul into numbered pieces, this data structure stores multiple values in indexed slots starting at zero.
hint: It starts at index 0 and holds items in order. Accessible with square brackets [].

riddle: The Marauder's Map tracks every footstep at Hogwarts. In the developer world, this tool tracks every change in your code — who wrote it, when, and why.
hint: Linus Torvalds created it. You 'commit', 'push', and 'pull' with it.

riddle: Like Dumbledore's Pensieve stores memories for quick access but clears when emptied, this computer component offers lightning-fast, volatile temporary storage.
hint: It stands for Random Access Memory.

riddle: Lucy steps through the wardrobe and reveals a hidden world. In code, this simple function is the first spell every beginner learns — it reveals output on your screen.
hint: In Python it's print(), in Java it's System.out.____ln().

riddle: The Sorting Hat at Hogwarts examines students and places them in the right house. This algorithm does the same — arranging a messy collection into order.
hint: Bubble, Quick, and Merge are all famous types of this.

riddle: Like Dobby the house-elf who was freed when Harry gave him a sock, this type of software is freely available for anyone to use, modify, and share.
hint: Linux is a famous example. Opposite of proprietary. Two words: ____ Source.

riddle: Like a Boggart that shapeshifts into whatever form it needs, this OOP concept lets one interface take many forms — a single method behaving differently for different objects.
hint: Poly = many, morph = forms. A pillar of Object-Oriented Programming.

riddle: Owls deliver messages between wizards across great distances. In tech, this is how different software systems talk to each other — sending requests and getting responses.
hint: Three letters. Application Programming Interface.

riddle: Like Nearly Headless Nick who wanders Hogwarts but has no physical body, this special value in code means a variable exists but points to absolutely nothing.
hint: In Java/JS it's ____; in Python it's None.

riddle: Hermione's Time-Turner lets her go back and redo things. In coding, this key command undoes your last action and takes you back to the previous state.
hint: Universal shortcut on Windows/Mac: Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z.

riddle: In Star Wars, the Force has only two sides — Light and Dark, On and Off, 1 and 0. Computers think entirely in this number system.
hint: It uses only two digits: 0 and 1. The word starts with 'bi'.

riddle: Like the Invisibility Cloak that hides Harry's details from the world, this OOP concept bundles data and methods while keeping internal implementation hidden.
hint: It's a pillar of OOP starting with 'E'. Think of enclosing data in a capsule.

riddle: Like Aragorn who inherits the throne and all powers of the King of Gondor, in OOP a child class receives all properties and methods from its parent class.
hint: One of the four pillars of OOP. A subclass ______s from a superclass.

riddle: In Westeros, maesters record history in scrolls. In code, this practice means writing human notes explaining what code does, completely ignored by the computer.
hint: In Python you use #, in JavaScript you use //. They are called ______s.

riddle: The massive Wall of the Night's Watch stands 700 feet high to keep wild threats out of Westeros. In networking, this barrier filters and blocks unauthorized traffic.
hint: A literal wall made of flame that protects your computer or network.

riddle: Doctor Strange traps Dormammu by creating a time loop that repeats and calls itself again and again until a base condition is finally met.
hint: A programming technique where a function calls itself.

riddle: Tony Stark stacks his Iron Man suits in vertical pods where the last suit placed inside is the first one deployed (LIFO). What data structure is this?
hint: Last-In, First-Out. Push and Pop are its signature operations.

riddle: Civilians fleeing an attack line up at the helicarrier: the first person to arrive is the first person rescued (FIFO). Which data structure follows this rule?
hint: First-In, First-Out. Used in printer jobs and message queues.

riddle: In The Matrix, operator monitors translate human thoughts into green digital code. In software, this program translates human source code into machine binary.
hint: GCC, Clang, and javac are famous examples.

riddle: Lando Calrissian oversees Cloud City high in Bespin's sky. In modern tech, this term describes running compute and storage on remote data centers across the internet.
hint: AWS, Azure, and Google ______.

riddle: Like the giant wooden horse that Greek soldiers hid inside to sneak into Troy, this malware disguises itself as legitimate, harmless software to trick users.
hint: Named after the legendary horse: a ______ Horse.

riddle: J.A.R.V.I.S. and F.R.I.D.A.Y. store petabytes of Avengers files and blueprints in structured tables queried in milliseconds. What system manages this organized data?
hint: SQL, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and MySQL are popular types of this.

riddle: Eleven loves waffles, but web browsers store these small crumbly pieces of data to remember your login and track your session across pages.
hint: A sweet baked snack name, but stored by your browser.

riddle: Luke and Han get trapped in the Death Star trash compactor where discarded junk is crushed. In Java and Python, this automatic process reclaims unused memory.
hint: Abbreviated as GC. It sweeps and frees objects that have no remaining references.

riddle: The Riddler leaves scrambled cyphers that only Batman can crack. In cybersecurity, this mathematical process scrambles plaintext into unreadable ciphertext.
hint: AES, RSA, and SSL all use this to protect sensitive passwords and traffic.

riddle: Cersei and Daenerys each hold a hostage and refuse to act until the other yields first, freezing all progress forever. In multithreading, what is this frozen state called?
hint: Occurs when two threads wait indefinitely for locks held by each other.
